newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 10.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
AKALI DAL-BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY COMBINE SWEEPS POLL

The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) alliance swept to power in Punjab. It was heading towards a three-fourths majority in the 117-seat assembly, as the ruling Congress was wiped out in the election. The SAD-BJP combine bagged 74 out of the 91 seats and was ahead in 27 other segments, as counting was still in progress for the remaining constituencies. The combine's rival, the Congress party, which won a majority in the 1992 poll with a rich haul of 87 seats, had won only 10 seats so far.
The Economic Times
VIDEOCON DROPS DIVERSIFICATION PLANS

The 19.24 billion rupee Videocon group dropped all its diversification plans. It would now concentrate on strengthening its existing consumer electronics business and getting its ventures in real estate development, power and petroleum off the ground. It opted out of the bidding process for Delhi's high speed tram system and has dropped plans to set up a colour picture tube facility. On the construction and real estate side, the group dropped plans to get into highway and road construction as well as plans to further its real estate development business. It would now pursue business only in the construction area.
NO CEILIING ON NON-RESIDENT INDIAN STAKE

Non-Resident Indian (NRI) investment in the domestic civil aviation sector would be treated as distinct from the 40 percent ceiling on foreign investment decided by the government. Consequently, there could be foreign investment of 40 percent and an additional NRI investment of 60 percent in a civil aviation venture, effectively allowing 100 percent investment in dollar terms. This was expected to be part of the modified aviation policy being worked out by the Civil Aviation Ministry. The new guideline was cleared by the Finance Ministry.
CENTRAL BANK ADVOCATES HIGHER SAVINGS TO SUSTAIN GROWTH

The budgetary deficit, as measured on January 24, 1997, was already more than double of that estimated for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). At 137.55 billion rupees, the deficit overshot the budget estimate of 65.78 billion rupees. The RBI was also concerned over the slowdown in industrial growth, high interest rates (both nominal and real) and a decline in the export growth rate in current financial year. Apart from these worrying trends, the central bank felt there was a need to further raise the savings rate for sustaining the economic growth rate at seven percent.
FORD TO SET UP FIVE BLN RUPEE COMPONENTS VENTURE

Ford Motor Co would set up two auto component ventures at an investment of five billion rupees to meet the export obligations of its car venture, Mahindra Ford India (MFIL). Ford also planned to set up an Indian holding company to route its future investments. The agreement with the government stipulated Mahindra Ford to export an equivalent amount of its imports to achieve foreign exchange neutrality in the project. For the first venture, Ford would invest 2.16 billion rupees over a seven-year period in a wholly-owned company that would manufacture components such as alternators and starters. The new company would be owned directly by Ford or the holding company.
Financial Express
EIGHTEEN INDUSTRIES REGISTER SLUMP IN OUTPUT

A survey conducted by an apex industry body, CII, showed 18 industries with a slump in production in April-December 1996. Nineteen sectors showed growth of less than 10 percent while only 16 sectors achieved a growth of more than 20 percent. The LPG, petrol, diesel, steel, pulp and paper, cotton yarn, nylon tyre yarn, water cooler, automobile tyres, thermal power, cigarettes and tobacco and rubber footwear industries regisrtered low growth. The survey covered CII member-firms and 56 affiliated associations, accounting for more than 65 percent of the total industry output.
FULL PROVISION FOR PAY REPORT IN BUDGET

The Finance Ministry would make a 112.5 billion rupee budgetary provision for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). This would be done to meet the expenditure to be incurred in implementing the pay panel's recommendations. The government would try to offset the resultant fiscal pressure by earmarking 90 billion rupees as accruals from the disinvestment programme in select government firms (PSUs).
Business Standard
INFLATION MOVES UP TO 7.7 PERCENT

The annual rate of inflation, after a brief spell of cessation in price rise, moved up again to touch 7.66 percent in the week ended January 25, 1997. Annual inflation (provisional-over-final) rose by 0.18 percentage point against 7.48 percent in the previous week even as the wholesale prices index for all commodities (base 1981/82) declined to 320.3 from 320.4 in the previous week. This was the 96th week in succession that inflation has maintained single digit levels.
ENRON READY TO INVEST $10 BILLION

Enron Corp of the United States has submitted a $10 billion proposal to the prime minister for five to seven power plants that would generate 10,000 megawatts. However, the company's insistence on a counter-guarantee from the government could be a tricky issue. The plan envisaged setting up five to seven power plants, with capacities ranging from 1,000 to 2,000 mw, in northern India as well as along the coastline in southern states.
The Observer
MULTINATIONALS RESTIVE OVER OIL SECTOR DEREGULATION DELAY

The procrastination in deregulating the oil sector is giving anxious moments to many foreign oil majors planning to invest in the country. The government has yet to take a decision on the deregulation despite an expert panel's recommendations in this regard. The firms are now eying Southeast Asia and China for future investment.
FOREIGN INVESTMENT BOOM ON THE CARDS IN MINING

The government envisages large private investments, including foreign capital, in the exploration and mining fields due to new mineral policies. The Mines Minister said the response of foreign mining firms, particularly British and Australian companies, was most enthusiastic. He said 36 proposals of foreign investment in the mining sector involving $500 million were cleared by the foreign investment promotion board. He said strategies were being formulated for greater mineral exploration using direct investment.
Business Line
HARD DECISIONS LIKELY IN BUDGET PREPARATION

The government indicated some hard decisions would be taken while evolving a pro-poor budget within the ambit of its common minimum programme. It took stock of the critical economic issues confronting it, including the mounting debt servicing burden, the spiralling oil pool deficit and the streamlining of the modified public distribution system. The government hinted it would introduce an economic package that would ensure higher investments in social infrastructure and agriculture in line with its basic minimum needs programme.
PETROLEUM GOODS PRICE HIKE ON CARDS

The government plans to start the process of structural reforms in the hydrocarbon sector by effecting a 12-15 percent across-the-board increase in price of key petroleum products within a fortnight. This will be followed by a partial dismantling of the administered pricing mechanism in the budget for 1997/98 (April-March). Some of the key products that were to be affected by the marginal price hike were liquefied petroleum gas, petrol, high speed diesel and aviation turbine fuel. Kerosene, though highly subsidised, was being left untouched in deference to the concerns of the ruling coalition's constituents.
